Browning, historian Holocaust scholar Raul Hilberg declared there were only two great Holocaust heroes -- the leader of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising (Mordechai Anielewicz) and Rudolf Vrba. After he escaped from Auschwitz-Birkenau in April of 1944, Vrba and his co-escapee Alfr d Wetzler co-authored the Vrba-Wetzler Report, credited with saving 200,000 Hungarian Jews. "No other single act in the Second World War," according to World War II historian Sir Martin Gilbert, "saved so many Jews from the fate that Hitler and the SS had determined for them." As one of the 20th century's most important whistleblowers, Vrba also stands out in Claude Lanzmann's Shoah as a handsome, charismatic and cheerful iconoclast. But the Yad Vashem Holocaust Museum in Israel has limited public awareness of Vrba because he consistently criticized Jewish leaders for failing to adequately forewarn Jews of their fate.
